report:
The complete retained P16.1 theorem is established relative to the mathematical bodies expressly granted by the task. The new argument establishes their outstanding application and countability antecedents; the conclusion is therefore not merely conditional on target envelope regularity. The verified scope is all dimensions, every algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, every reduced irreducible geometrically unibranch projective variety, including nonnormal varieties, and every actual ample rational line bundle.

I used the supplied mathematical bodies and binding clarifications for the grant-scope checks and opened the version-pinned Temkin, Boucksom–Jonsson, Boucksom–Eriksson and Wu primary papers. Historical acceptance labels, the previous review, compilation and hashes supplied no mathematical evidence. Task-granted assumptions are excluded from the external-premise list below.

The grants retain distinct scopes. The contact body supplies the model-first construction for the specified already-glued weights and bounded collars, with the full potential p+Ψ/A. The actual86 bodies supply local conversion on the actual semiample bundle without target EP, the precisely quantified countable-to-arbitrary-field implication, and the general-variety equation deduction after target EP. The actual87 body supplies geometric completions, domination of the specified original witness and exact-infimum sequence extraction. The actual88 bodies supply all-point fiber constancy and the normalization-factorization argument. The repaired actual89 bodies supply the entire original-ring affine chain and its original-reference projective consequence. None of these grants separately supplies the new join.

The resolution application meets Temkin's hypotheses: the original integral variety is Noetherian, excellent and generically reduced over Q. The blowups retain its function field and yield an integral smooth projective source. Connectedness is obtained on the normal base before passing through the universal homeomorphism to the original target. The fiber argument retains the fixed actual M and A references, the signed curve-current identity, boundary Green corrections and bounded floors. Its comparison of arbitrary analytic points uses residue-field lifts and curve chains, rather than density plus upper semicontinuity. Consequently the descended scalar is defined at every point, is usc and bounded above, and is finite at the generic trivial valuation. These conclusions do not assert target psh membership prematurely.

The local contact application matches the affine theorem. The original homogeneous ratios generate each original chart ring, and ρ_i is exactly its canonical reference weight. Each restricted witness remains proper birational over that chart. Local compact generator bounds have ordinary interiors; the pulled frames and ample perturbations stay fixed throughout conversion. Finite winning branches give unit-log supports with the same constants, and floors cover zero branches. Countability permits increasing-index extraction with the exact pointwise infimum, including −∞; cofinality is unnecessary. Restrictions, positive combinations, maxima, logarithmic floors and products retain the prescribed witness and references. The boundary blowup formula supplies an effective ample divisor with the complete boundary support. Relative Chow, closure and resolution retain domination of the whole witness over the original affine base. Common domination is used only for finitely many witnesses.

The repaired affine proof also preserves its essential qualifications. Trace weights are positive norm-law multiplicities, including at nonflat fibers; the bad-fiber argument lifts to the same witness using relative properness. Pole control passes through finite normalization and does not assert that integral functions belong to the original ring. Both Rossi applications use a neighborhood containing the tested point. The split argument retains one common base neighborhood and treats γ=1 separately. Product Runge precedes Hartogs, whose radius formula retains the strict constant-coefficient conditions. The descending bad strata strictly lose dimension, and the final empty-stratum product argument supplies affine globalization. None of these operations needs unproved target EP.

First genuine target membership follows from that matched application. Whole-boundary collars on the original projective variety give ψ−(c−1)ρ_i in the actual class cL, extended by −∞ outside its chart. Their finite maximum equals ψ everywhere because a maximal homogeneous coordinate has ρ_i=0. Varying-class decreasing closure applies to the constant scalar family ψ as c decreases to one; it is not applied to the individually increasing chart extensions. Only afterward does fiber constancy yield onto pullback. The common divisorial coordinates give both directions of the homeomorphism, while analytic surjectivity preserves actual suprema. Smooth-source nef compactness and general BJ 5.11 then establish target EP throughout the entire countable domain required by actual86.

The arbitrary-cardinality step retains nonnormal descent and the actual polarization. The descended finite normal birational algebra is the actual normalization, and the universal-homeomorphism property descends faithfully flatly. Analytic restriction is surjective, with the enlarged ground field remaining trivially valued. Each finite competitor receives its own enlarged countable field and its own actual generating-section representation. Continuous raw cycle pushforward transfers the nonnegative orthogonality integral. Domination requires neither target EP nor inverse-equation existence. Compact closed-set tail extraction handles arbitrary genuine competitors without descending an entire psh family. Thus the envelope identity is exact, and continuity and EP extend to the original arbitrary field. General compactness supplies actual psh potentials even when the normalized space is nonmetrizable.

The operator is the genuine general-projective intersection operator. Relative integral closure retains the original generic fiber; central coefficients b_E and fundamental-cycle multiplicities remain present. Positive PL test functionals extend to actual positive Radon measures with raw intersection mass. Finite mixed energy and the signed multilinear extension justify unbounded tests. Genuine decreasing nets with finite-energy endpoints give weak mixed convergence; weighted convergence uses the test-containing pairing minus the zero-test pairing, followed by the positive weighted-measure lemma. Differences of decreasing tests are handled term by term. No undefined subtraction of two −∞ values is used.

Raw and probability calibration is consistent: E_raw=V E_BJ, MA_raw=V MA_BJ, and E_raw∨(μ)=V E_BJ∨(μ/V). The integrability characterization concerns every genuine E1 potential. Its converse produces an actual decreasing finite-energy sum and uses the quadratic J estimate to bound the dual supremum. The uniform PL outer derivative passes to unbounded potentials, and uniform approximation of continuous directions has errors |t|ε. Both derivative signs are checked. Strict-winning locality and displaced maxima give comparison; the general equidimensional uniqueness and domination arguments apply because the target is irreducible. Divisorial Dirac finite energy is used independently of an inverse Dirac equation.

Existence is attained in genuine E1. A normalized maximizing sequence has bounded J; original-target compactness gives a convergent subnet to an actual psh potential. Lower semicontinuity of J makes that potential finite energy. Target L1 continuity and energy upper semicontinuity establish attainment of the intrinsic dual supremum. Envelope variations remain between bounded translates of the maximizer and therefore remain genuine E1. Positive and negative variations identify its raw measure against dense PL tests, hence against every continuous test. Equal measures imply equality modulo one real constant. There is no support, invariance or skeleton restriction beyond intrinsic finite dual energy.

Normalization transport is correctly postponed until approaching target classes have EP. Onto psh pullback, extended pairing identities and degree-one cycle projection then establish onto E1, unchanged raw mass, all stated unbounded mixed and integrable weighted limits, and equality of intrinsic dual suprema. Scalar descent alone is never used to infer finite-energy equivalence for the resolution's nonample pulled class.

The pertinent elementary source corrections are harmless and can be checked directly. BJ 3.10 uses convex interpolation between the nef and ample model classes; BJ 7.30's telescoping sum runs from 0 through n−1; BJ 7.33's first bound includes the factor t. The weighted identity in BJ 7.21(ii) has the test pairing first. The absolute-difference identity in BJ 9.19 has a minus sign. Continuous-direction approximation in BJ 8.6 uses |t|ε and an upper error +ε. The locality limit uses weighted convergence, and BJ 12.8's compactness citation is general 5.11 under EP. The arithmetic inequality behind strict concavity follows directly from a(1−t)^2+bt^2≥0. BE 8.6's last expanded difference has a minus sign; its absolute-value estimate is unchanged. Geometric witness maps are understood over the original affine base, with smooth projective source, without asserting a smooth morphism. These corrections require no change to the claimed theorem or substantive new construction.

Wu v1's envelope proof was checked: it explicitly calls its fiber-descent and weak/global gates before field enlargement. Its printed theorem was not substituted for the new join. The draft supplies the granted replacements and uses the orthogonality integral, avoiding the printed inverse-support equality.

Dimension zero is established directly: X=Spec k, V=1, E_raw(a)=a, and the only mass-one target is the unit point measure. All finite potentials differ by constants. Binding identifiers remain distinct from hashes of delimiter-inclusive preserved copies; alternate serialization does not change mathematical scope. The final verified theorem covers the full retained P16.1 domain and makes no claim about the other P16 axes.

passages.quote: the centers of the blow ups are disjoint from the preimages of the regular locus

passages.statement: Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, conventions and §§2–4: over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, a variety may be reduced and nonnormal. On a reduced projective variety, canonical evaluation gives |s|≤1 for global sections, and a generating section system has maximum canonical norm one at every analytic point. Rational PL functions are uniformly dense in C0. For an actual ample rational L, Hdom(c1(L))⊂H(L); every genuine L-psh potential is a decreasing net limit in Hdom(c1(L)), and every continuous genuine L-psh potential is a uniform limit on that same actual bundle. Genuine psh cones admit constants in nef classes, finite maxima in one class, positive sums with corresponding class sums, and decreasing varying-class limits whenever the limit is generically finite. Dominant pullback between integral projective varieties preserves genuine psh potentials. Nef potentials admit decreasing finite rational Fubini–Study approximants in ample classes approaching the nef class. These approximation and closure assertions require no envelope property.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Proposition 4.12, Theorem 4.22, Corollary 4.23 and Proposition 4.28: on a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, genuine psh potentials are finite on divisorial valuations and uniquely determined there. For genuine ϕ and usc ψ, inequality on divisorial valuations implies inequality everywhere. The topology of divisorial pointwise convergence is Hausdorff, and ϕ↦sup(ϕ−f) is continuous for fixed real PL f. On an irreducible variety, sup ϕ equals its generic trivial-valuation value.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 5.11, Lemmas 5.13 and 5.17, Theorem 5.20 and Corollary 5.21: on an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, a numerical class has the envelope property exactly when its sup-normalized genuine psh space is compact in the divisorial topology. For an ample class, EP is equivalent to continuity of envelopes of all continuous obstacles; envelopes obey the uniform Lipschitz inequality. On a smooth connected projective variety every nef class has EP and normalized compactness. If π:Y→X is birational and θ is approached by target classes θ_m having EP with θ_m−θ ample, genuine pullback PSH(X,θ)→PSH(Y,π*θ) is an onto homeomorphism.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 5.11, Lemmas 5.13 and 5.17, Theorem 5.20 and Corollary 5.21: on an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, a numerical class has the envelope property exactly when its sup-normalized genuine psh space is compact in the divisorial topology. For an ample class, EP is equivalent to continuity of envelopes of all continuous obstacles; envelopes obey the uniform Lipschitz inequality. On a smooth connected projective variety every nef class has EP and normalized compactness. If π:Y→X is birational and θ is approached by target classes θ_m having EP with θ_m−θ ample, genuine pullback PSH(X,θ)→PSH(Y,π*θ) is an onto homeomorphism.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorems 7.1, 7.8, 7.14 and 7.18 and Propositions 7.2, 7.7, 7.19 and 7.21: on a reduced projective variety X of dimension n over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field, the intersection energy pairing for ample psh entries extends uniquely as a symmetric increasing usc pairing into R∪{−∞}, continuous along genuine decreasing nets. E_ω(ϕ)=(ω,ϕ)^(n+1)/((n+1)(ω^n)) is concave, increasing, usc and decreasing-net continuous. Its finite-energy cone contains bounded psh potentials, is convex and upward closed within PSH, and has finite mixed pairings. Differences of finite-energy potentials on the linear-growth locus admit the compatible signed multilinear pairing. Mixed products of ample genuine finite-energy entries are positive Radon measures of raw mass (ω_1⋯ω_n). On relatively integrally closed test configurations retaining the original generic fiber, their PL formula has coefficients ord_E(X_0)·((ω_1,X+D_1)|E⋯(ω_n,X+D_n)|E). Mixed measures converge weakly along genuine decreasing nets with finite-energy endpoints. Genuine finite-energy tests are integrable against finite-energy mixed measures. More generally, an integrable psh test ϕ_0 and decreasing psh approximants to all entries satisfy ϕ_0j μ_j→ϕ_0 μ weakly; its integral is the test-containing pairing minus the zero-test pairing. Energy pairings and raw mixed measures are compatible with normalization pullback and pushforward for pulled genuine potentials, without requiring onto pullback.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Proposition 8.3, Theorem 8.5 and Corollary 8.6: on a reduced projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field with ample ω, the outer energy E↓, defined using continuous majorants, is increasing, concave, translation equivariant, agrees with E on genuine psh potentials, and is continuous along decreasing upper-bounded usc nets. Under EP it equals E(P(u)) for upper-bounded usc u whenever the envelope is genuine. For fixed real PL f and every ϕ∈E1(ω), E↓(ϕ+tf)=E(ϕ)+t∫f MA_ω(ϕ)+O_f(t²), with the error constant uniform in ϕ. For every continuous f the two-sided derivative at zero is ∫f MA_ω(ϕ). Here MA_ω is probability normalized.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, §§7.4, 9 and Proposition 11.1: let X be irreducible projective of positive dimension over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field and ω ample. For a Radon probability measure μ, E∨(μ)=sup_{ϕ∈E1}(E(ϕ)−∫ϕ μ) is finite exactly when every genuine E1 potential is μ-integrable. Put J(ϕ)=sup ϕ−E(ϕ), D=E∨(μ), and J_μ(ϕ)=D−E(ϕ)+∫ϕ μ. For finite D, J(ϕ)≤C_n(J_μ(ϕ)+D). Maximizing genuine E1 nets have MA measures converging weakly to μ. Weak convergence of genuine psh potentials with eventually bounded J implies L1(μ) convergence for every finite-dual-energy μ. The energy inequalities give I≥0, I–J comparability, strict concavity and J(tϕ)≤C_n t²J(ϕ) for normalized ϕ and 0≤t≤1. Every divisorial Dirac measure has finite dual energy. These assertions do not assume EP or inverse-equation existence.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorems 7.40 and 7.44, Corollary 7.41 and Corollaries 10.4–10.6: on an irreducible projective variety over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field with ample ω, genuine E1 potentials satisfy strict-winning locality 1_{ϕ>ψ}MA(max(ϕ,ψ))=1_{ϕ>ψ}MA(ϕ) and comparison ∫_{ϕ<ψ}MA(ψ)≤∫_{ϕ<ψ}MA(ϕ). Mixed finite-energy products agree on an open set where their corresponding potentials agree. Equality of MA measures is equivalent to I(ϕ,ψ)=0 and to ϕ−ψ being one real constant. If a∈PSH(ω), b∈E1(ω), and a≤b almost everywhere for MA(b), then a≤b everywhere. These statements require no EP.

Boucksom–Jonsson, arXiv:1801.08229v4, Theorem 12.8 and Theorem 13.1: let X be irreducible projective over an algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero field and ω ample. If ω has EP, the genuine finite-energy MA operator is onto all Radon probability measures of finite intrinsic dual energy, and the dual supremum for each such measure is attained by an actual genuine E1 potential. For every continuous obstacle f, p=P_ω(f) is continuous genuine psh and satisfies ∫(f−p) MA_ω(p)=0. No smoothness or support hypothesis is imposed on X or the finite-energy target.

Boucksom–Eriksson, arXiv:1805.01016v3, Theorem 7.14, Proposition 8.3, Theorem 8.4, Proposition 8.5 and Theorem 8.18: on a geometrically reduced projective scheme over any complete non-Archimedean field, including a trivially valued field, psh metrics on actual semiample rational line bundles admit decreasing smooth semipositive regularization; for continuous metrics the convergence is uniform. Mixed measures of smooth semipositive metrics are positive Radon measures defined with the analytic fundamental cycle and have raw intersection mass. They commute by pushforward with every complete-field extension. They extend uniquely to continuous psh-regularizable metrics by uniform-to-weak continuity, retaining positivity, symmetry, multilinearity and raw intersection mass. For model metrics on fixed actual bundles on a flat projective model, the metric on their Deligne pairing is the corresponding model Deligne-pairing metric. BJ Remark 7.23 identifies the resulting continuous mixed operator with its intersection-energy operator.
